extracted.intended_audience: conference organizers, machine-learning researchers, and developers of paper-reviewer matching systems
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, implementing, and evaluating an automated conference paper–reviewer matching system (TPMS) that estimates reviewer expertise and produces reviewer assignments under conference constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise estimation per paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine reviewers’ expertise with respect to each submission (i.e., evaluate the expertise of every reviewer with respect to each submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reviewers’ previous publications (reviewer archive) and submitted papers to build representations and compute scores; scores are used to rank candidate reviewers and drive elicitation and matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching constraints: reviews per paper (Rtarget)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper must be reviewed by a certain number of reviewers (Rtarget).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce as a hard constraint in the assignment optimization (e.g., sum_r y_rp = Rtarget for all p).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching constraints: reviewer load limit (Pmax)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reviewer has a limit on the number of papers they can review (Pmax).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce as a hard constraint in the assignment optimization (e.g., sum_p y_rp ≤ Pmax for all r) to balance load.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts-of-interest and global constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Global constraints such as conflicts of interest must be respected when assigning reviewers to papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate conflict information into the matching problem so assignments that violate COI are forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment utility maximization objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize assignments by maximizing total reviewer–paper utility: maximize Σ_{r,p} s_rp * y_rp where s_rp is reviewer expertise score and y_rp is assignment indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this linear objective as the primary optimization; other non-linear utility variants have been explored (Charlin et al., 2011).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reviewer bids vs. self-assessed scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between reviewers’ bids (interest) and self-assessed expertise scores (expertise); prefer expertise scores to estimate suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TPMS uses self-assessed scores to predict missing scores and may combine bids and scores in supervised models; bids represent interest, scores represent expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial (unsupervised) scoring from archives
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute initial scores from reviewer archives and submissions without elicited scores (e.g., language-model dot product or topic representations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These initial scores can be computed before submission deadlines and used to guide active elicitation and early matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language Model similarity (word-LM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Predict a reviewer’s score as the dot product between a reviewer’s archive representation and a submission representation using normalized word counts (srp = f(Ar) f(Pp)′).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Dirichlet smoothing for reviewer normalized counts; consider normalizing scores by paper length to avoid bias toward short papers; alternatives include KL-divergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-space representation (LDA / topic-LM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent archives and submissions in topic space (LDA) and compute expertise scores using topic distributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning topics can abstract away stylistic noise; TPMS used 30 topics for experiments; topic-LM often separates a top few reviewers more clearly than word-LM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervised score prediction (per-reviewer regressions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Train separate linear regression models per reviewer to predict scores from submission features: srp = θ_r f(Pp)′.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works well when many elicited scores per reviewer are available; can be trained online; regularization and feature choices matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter sharing across reviewers (LR-shared)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow parameter sharing between users and papers to handle reviewers with few or no observed scores: srp = b + b_r + (θ + θ_p) f(Pp)′ + (ω + ω_r) g(Ar)′.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared parameters (θ, ω) capture global feature weights; per-reviewer and per-paper terms capture idiosyncrasies; tune regularizers so shared parameters are learned robustly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative filtering baseline (PMF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use probabilistic matrix factorization (PMF) to model scores as low-rank dot products (srp = θ_r ω_p′) without side information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PMF performs poorly in cold-start regimes; remains an interesting baseline; tune rank and use gradient-based training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling cold-start reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Models must handle reviewers with very few or zero observed scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parameter sharing, side-information from archives, and global models; re-use archives across conferences where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active expertise elicitation guided by uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Guide score elicitation (queries to reviewers) using model uncertainty/utility (e.g., query reviewer-paper pairs with high informativeness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TPMS used inverse entropy of the distribution across area chairs per paper to pick papers for elicitation; adapt number of elicited scores per user via matching constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elicitation bias awareness (scores not missing at random)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that elicited scores will be biased by the matching constraints (i.e., not missing at random) because queries target assignments the system expects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This bias is acceptable for assignment tasks (informative queries), but should be acknowledged when evaluating models; consider methods robust to MNAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization of scores by paper length
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalize predicted scores by submission length to avoid systematic biases (shorter papers tending to receive higher similarity scores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using dot-product between bag-of-words representations, normalization helps produce fairer ranked lists and comparability across submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dirichlet smoothing for archive word counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Smooth reviewer archive word counts using a Dirichlet prior to better handle rare words in the language model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use f(Ar_w) = (N_Ar / (N_Ar + μ)) * (|w_Ar| / N_Ar) + (μ / (N_Ar + μ)) * (|w| / N) with suitable μ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating initial-score quality with ranking metrics (NDCG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare top-ranked reviewer lists from different initial scoring methods using ranking metrics like NDCG@k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TPMS compared word-LM vs topic-LM by measuring average NDCG@5 and NDCG@10 across datasets (high NDCG indicates similar rankings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating score-prediction with RMSE
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the accuracy of predicted expertise scores against elicited ground truth using RMSE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-validation (e.g., 5-fold), tune hyperparameters on validation fold; report means and standard errors; compare LR, LR-shared, PMF and constant baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate assignment quality indirectly via score prediction and in-vivo experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Because ground-truth optimal assignments are unavailable, evaluate system effectiveness via (a) score-prediction performance, (b) ranking similarity, and (c) in-vivo experiments within conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-vivo experiments (e.g., showing ranked lists to reviewers and polling interface usefulness) provide practical assessment but may include biases from the ranking method used to present lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce personalized ranked lists for program committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide area chairs and reviewers with ranked candidate lists to help select reviewers and prioritize papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use predicted scores to sort reviewers per paper; area chairs may vet these lists or use them to guide assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software integration with conference management (CMT) via SWORD/APP
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate with conference management systems (e.g., Microsoft CMT) through an API using standard protocols such as SWORD/Atom Publishing Protocol for exchanging submissions, reviewer info, and elicited scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TPMS communicates via SWORD messages: deposit documents, send reviewer metadata and bids, and return computed scores; integration reduces organizer burden but requires engineering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated reviewer archive harvesting and reviewer interface
rubrics_metrics.description: Support harvesting reviewers’ published papers automatically (URLs, Google Scholar crawling) and allow reviewers to upload PDFs to build their archives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing easy archive population reduces manual effort; conference organizers can also populate archives on reviewers’ behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability and time constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: System must produce assignments within tight conference time windows (a couple of days after submission deadline) and scale to thousands of submissions and hundreds of reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute initial expertise before submission deadlines where possible; automate pipeline (crawler, feature extraction, model training) and optimize matching performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reuse of reviewer archives (and possibly scores) across conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-use previously harvested reviewer archives across multiple conferences; consider re-using elicited scores as part of reviewer profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A central system can leverage cross-conference data to improve cold-start handling and reduce per-conference setup cost; consider privacy and consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data anonymization and data release practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Properly anonymize and consider releasing gathered data to support reproducible research while protecting reviewers’ privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymize reviewer identities and sensitive metadata before public release; obtain necessary permissions from conferences and reviewers where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve integration and reduce per-conference tailoring cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimize per-conference manual tailoring by offering a base system that can be extended with minimal help, or by keeping a centrally hosted system that conferences can use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade-offs: local downloads reduce dependencies but increase organizer work; a hosted system simplifies use and enables data reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active elicitation trade-offs and elicitation budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Design elicitation strategies that choose which reviewer–paper pairs to query, balancing number of queries per reviewer and overall information gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt the number of queries per user according to matching constraints and use uncertainty measures (e.g., inverse entropy) to pick informative queries; practical experiments used two elicitation rounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection and validation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cross-validation splits, hyper-parameter tuning, and appropriate training algorithms (VW, BFGS, gradient descent) to select and validate models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Split datasets (e.g., 5-fold), tune on validation fold(s), and compare multiple candidate models (LR, LR-shared, PMF) reporting RMSE and other metrics with error bars.
